podcast.title: Mother's Murder (March 3, 1983) – Boyfriend John "Dean" Ricardi Shot Connie and Friend, Caught via America's Most Wanted
podcast.body: Dave Navarro was 15 years old when his mother Connie — one of the models on *Let's Make a Deal* with Monty Hall — was shot to death along with her best friend Sue by her ex-boyfriend, a bodybuilder named John Ricardi (who went by "Dean"). After the relationship deteriorated and Connie sought a restraining order, Ricardi broke into the house on the night of March 3, 1983, and waited. Dave narrowly escaped by spending the weekend with his father. Ricardi evaded capture for almost eight years until a tip from a viewer of *America's Most Wanted* led to his arrest in Houston, Texas, on January 4, 1991. Dave testified against him at trial; Ricardi was subsequently placed on death row at San Quentin. "Human beings are not equipped to know how to handle something like that."

podcast.title: Long COVID Battle and Tour Withdrawal
podcast.body: Dave Navarro of Jane's Addiction contracted COVID-19 in late 2021, and although he recovered from the acute phase of the illness, he subsequently became a sufferer of long COVID. His symptoms, including severe fatigue and weakness, persisted for many months, forcing him to withdraw from Jane's Addiction's announced 32-day tour with The Smashing Pumpkins in late 2022. "And although he got through the worst of it, he's become a sufferer of long COVID."

xref.title: Dave Navarro's Recruitment (September 1993)
xref.body: Dave Navarro joined the Red Hot Chili Peppers in September 1993, replacing Jesse Tobias, who had been with the band for less than a year. Navarro had been courted by several bands after Jane's Addiction disbanded, including an offer from Guns N' Roses to replace Izzy Stradlin, which he declined. Although he initially doubted his suitability for the band's funky style, he was persuaded to join. xref.title: Dave Navarro's Dismissal (Spring 1998)
xref.body: Dave Navarro was fired in the spring of 1998 due to escalating personal and drug-related conflicts, particularly with Anthony Kiedis, who was attempting to get clean while Navarro was heavily using heroin. Navarro frequently arrived late and high for rehearsals, leading to an argumentative meeting where he fell backwards over an amplifier and stormed out. Bassist Flea's health and relationship issues also contributed to the decision to bring back John Frusciante, ultimately leading to Navarro's ousting. "Dave was out."

xref.title: Reaching Out to Frusciante for Reunion (1998)
xref.body: Following Dave Navarro's firing in April 1997, Anthony Kiedis made the initial move to reconnect with John Frusciante, visiting him at a gallery event where Frusciante's paintings were displayed. Recognizing Frusciante's recovery and lack of an instrument, Kiedis personally bought him a '62 Stratocaster to help him restart his musical journey and rejoin the Red Hot Chili Peppers. "Anthony was the first to reach out by going to a gallery event where John was displaying some of his paintings."

xref.title: Reunion with John Frusciante (1998)
xref.body: After Dave Navarro's firing in April 1997, Anthony Kiedis and Flea initiated contact with a recovering John Frusciante. Kiedis visited Frusciante's art gallery, and Flea personally invited him to rejoin the band, expressing great happiness at the prospect. Kiedis even purchased a '62 Stratocaster for Frusciante, who didn't own a guitar at the time. The reunited classic lineup began jamming, writing, and recording demos in Flea's garage in September 1998, signifying Frusciante's return after a six-year absence. "Anthony was the first to reach out by going to a gallery event where John was displaying some of his paintings."
